status: Referred to Joint Committee on Energy and Technology 2025-01-10; no further action recorded on the bill's CGA history; died in committee at 2025 regular session sine die adjournment 2025-06-04
key_provisions: Would require AI data centers to use at least 50 percent renewable energy, use storage and modern grid infrastructure, adopt water conservation measures, and report energy, water, and emissions data.

status: Joint Favorable 2026-03-19; filed with Legislative Commissioners' Office and reported out 2026-04-07 with File No. 421 and House Calendar No. 305 (Favorable Report, Tabled for the Calendar, House); never called for a House vote; died on the House calendar at 2026 regular session sine die adjournment 2026-05-06
key_provisions: Would regulate large electric load customers of at least 50 MW, require co-located electric supplier licensing, require new large-load tariffs, require 100 percent load coverage plus reserve margin from new generation subject to waivers, and require financial guarantees to protect other ratepayers.

status: Referred to Joint Committee on Energy and Technology 2025-01-22; no further action recorded; died in committee at 2025 regular session sine die adjournment 2025-06-04
key_provisions: Would create a surcharge on electricity consumed by data centers and use proceeds to offset the Combined Public Benefits Charge on residential utility bills.

status: Referred to Joint Committee on Energy and Technology 2025-01-22; no further action recorded; died in committee at 2025 regular session sine die adjournment 2025-06-04
key_provisions: Would require PURA, with OCC, DEEP, and ISO New England, to evaluate large data center impacts on electric distribution reliability.

status: Referred to Joint Committee on Finance, Revenue and Bonding 2024-02-14; no further action recorded; died in committee at 2024 regular session sine die adjournment 2024-05-08
key_provisions: Would eliminate chapter 203 and chapter 219 tax exemptions for qualified data centers.

sponsors: Energy and Technology Committee; co-sponsors Rep. Steven Winter, Rep. Bill Buckbee, Rep. Nick Gauthier, Sen. Martha Marx
party: Committee bill; bipartisan co-sponsors (Winter D, Buckbee R, Gauthier D, Marx D)
status: Joint Favorable Change of Reference to Committee on Finance, Revenue and Bonding 2026-03-17; re-referred to Finance, Revenue and Bonding 2026-03-23; no further committee or floor action recorded; died in committee at 2026 regular session sine die adjournment 2026-05-06
key_provisions: Would stop DECD from accepting new qualified data center tax incentive applications on or after 2026-07-01.

sponsors: Energy and Technology Committee; co-sponsor Rep. Mary Mushinsky
status: Joint Favorable Substitute 2025-03-18; filed with Legislative Commissioners' Office and reported out 2025-04-07 with File No. 538 and Senate Calendar No. 303 (Favorable Report, Tabled for the Calendar, Senate); never called for a Senate vote; died on the Senate calendar at 2025 regular session sine die adjournment 2025-06-04
key_provisions: Original bill would require AI data center quarterly reports and DEEP energy and water efficiency regulations; substitute bill would require a state study of AI data center energy efficiency requirements.

sponsors: Rep. Frank Burns; Sen. Stephanie Hansen; Rep. Debra Heffernan
status: Substituted by House Substitute 1 for HB 233 on 2026-05-21; substitute signed and effective 2026-08-26 (85 Del. Laws ch. 440).
key_provisions: Enacted House Substitute 1 covers large energy use facilities under alternative 75 MW/85%-load-factor, 100 MW instantaneous-demand, or 30 MW NAICS 518210 thresholds, with aggregation and specified exclusions. Requires utility rate classifications and service/security agreements to allocate costs and protect reliability. The 180-day rate-filing deadline runs from finalization of Commission regulations, not enactment.

sponsors: Sen. Stephanie Hansen; Sen. Nicole Poore; Rep. Frank Burns; Rep. Debra Heffernan; Rep. Eric Morrison; others
status: 153rd General Assembly ended with final recorded status Out of Committee 2026-03-11; not enacted. Official bill page displays no floor roll-call records.
key_provisions: As introduced, required a Public Service Commission certificate to operate for facilities using 30 MW or more. Senate Amendment 1, introduced 2026-01-28, would change the threshold to 100 MW, frame the certificate as a transmission certificate, add distribution-company requirements, and add water-supply review.

sponsors: Sen. Poore; Rep. Burns; Rep. Heffernan; Rep. Minor-Brown; others
status: Signed and effective 2026-08-26 (85 Del. Laws ch. 447).
key_provisions: Amends Title 9, Title 22, and Title 29 of the Delaware Code relating to data centers. Prohibits state agencies, counties, and municipalities from entering into nondisclosure agreements that would restrict public access to information about potential or actual large-scale data center development (defined by reference to facilities capable of using 100+ MW), aiming to preserve local transparency and public input into data-center siting decisions.
